annotation.speech2: A point P 0 surrounded by a dashed unit circle of possible directions. A long red arrow shows the gradient of f. A blue unit arrow shows a direction u making an angle theta with the gradient. Two gray arrows orthogonal to the gradient mark the directions of zero change. Below the circle is the formula: the directional derivative equals the magnitude of the gradient times cosine theta.
The gradient vector of f at P 0, drawn in red. Moving in this direction gives the most rapid increase, with directional derivative equal to the magnitude of the gradient.
A unit vector u, drawn in blue, making an angle theta with the gradient. Its directional derivative is the magnitude of the gradient times cosine theta.
A direction orthogonal to the gradient, where cosine theta is zero, so the directional derivative is zero and f does not change.
The opposite orthogonal direction, where the directional derivative is also zero.
The dashed unit circle of all possible directions u at the point P 0.
